# NYU SPS — MS in Management and Analytics
## Professor Research Directory

**Purpose:** Identify professors associated with each course, understand their academic and professional backgrounds, explore their specialisations, and find their LinkedIn profiles to prepare for the programme.

**Programme:** MS in Management and Analytics  
**School:** NYU School of Professional Studies (NYU SPS)

> **Research note:** Faculty affiliations and course associations should not be treated as confirmation of teaching assignments for a specific semester. Verify the instructor against the actual course section and term before relying on the information.

## 3. Professor Profiles

### 3.1 Dr. Andrew D. Banasiewicz

**Position:** Clinical Professor  
**Department:** Management and Technology

**Courses associated with his NYU SPS faculty profile:**
- MASY1-GC1015 — Quantitative Methods for Business Analysis
- MASY1-GC2000 — Foundations of Business Analytics
- MASY1-GC2200 — Foundations of Risk Analytics
- MASY1-GC4115 — Applied Technical Project

**Academic and professional background**

Dr. Banasiewicz is an academic and analytics practitioner whose areas of expertise include business analytics, risk-related applications and evidence-based decision-making.

**Areas to investigate**
- Quantitative analysis and business decision-making
- Risk analytics and analytical reasoning
- Applications of data in business strategy
- Publications and books on analytics
- Teaching approach and applied projects

**Why this professor is relevant**

His experience is particularly relevant to understanding how quantitative concepts are translated into practical business decisions and analytics projects.

### 3.2 Rajeev Maharaj

**Position:** Adjunct Instructor  
**Department:** Division of Programs in Business

**Courses associated with his NYU SPS faculty profile:**
- MASY1-GC1015 — Quantitative Methods for Business Analysis
- MASY1-GC2100 — Advanced Business Analytics

**Academic and professional background**

His NYU SPS biography describes experience across financial institutions, including the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Citi, Morgan Stanley and Volkswagen Credit. His experience includes quantitative finance, risk management, machine learning and applied AI.

His educational background includes master's degrees in Risk Management and Business Analytics from NYU Stern.

**Areas to investigate**
- Quantitative finance
- Machine learning and applied AI
- Risk modelling and analytics
- Statistical methods
- Applications of analytics in financial services

**Why this professor is relevant**

His professional background can help connect statistical methods and machine learning concepts with real-world business and financial applications.

Use the following template for every professor identified during the research.

### Professor Name

- **Official title:**
- **Department:**
- **Courses taught:**
- **Confirmed teaching assignment for my term:**
- **Official NYU faculty profile:**
- **Verified LinkedIn profile:**

#### Academic Background
- Undergraduate qualifications
- Postgraduate qualifications

- Research interests
- Publications

#### Professional Background
- Current role
- Previous employers
- Leadership positions
- Industry experience
- Relevant projects

#### Subject-Matter Specialisation
- Primary areas of expertise
- Secondary areas of expertise
- Research topics
- Relevant industry applications

#### Teaching and Assessment
- Courses previously taught
- Publicly documented teaching approach
- Available syllabi and course materials
- Publicly documented assessment methods
- Relevant case studies or projects

#### LinkedIn Research
- Verified profile URL
- Current professional role
- Career history
- Public posts and publications
- Relevant professional interests

#### Preparation Recommendations
- Prerequisite concepts
- Topics to learn before class
- Recommended reading
- Relevant software or technical skills
- Practice exercises
- Questions to ask the professor

## 6. Research Priorities

Prioritise the professors and courses that will help establish your technical foundations.

| Priority | Subject area | Preparation focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Quantitative Methods for Business Analysis | Algebra, descriptive statistics, probability and hypothesis testing |
| 2 | Database Management | Relational databases, tables, keys and introductory SQL |
| 3 | Foundations of Business Analytics | Data cleaning, descriptive analytics and visualisation |
| 4 | Data-Driven Decision-Making | Interpreting data, evaluating alternatives and communicating findings |
| 5 | Programming | Programming logic, variables, conditions, loops and functions |
| 6 | Managing Technical Projects | Project planning, Agile, stakeholders and risk |
| 7 | Advanced Analytics and Risk Analytics | Build on the mathematics and statistics foundations first |
| 8 | Research Methods and Applied Projects | Research questions, methodology and presenting evidence |

These priorities are a suggested preparation order, not an official NYU prerequisite sequence.

## 7. Verification Checklist

Before treating this directory as final, verify the following:

- [ ] Confirm the exact semester and year.
- [ ] Confirm the current programme curriculum.
- [ ] Confirm the course codes and titles.
- [ ] Check the actual instructor assigned to each registered section.
- [ ] Distinguish current teaching assignments from historical assignments.
- [ ] Verify each LinkedIn profile against the professor's official name and professional history.
- [ ] Review official faculty biographies and relevant publications.
- [ ] Locate current syllabi and assessment information where publicly available.
- [ ] Update the directory when registration or instructor assignments change.

---

## 8. Important Research Limitations

This document is a preliminary faculty research directory. It should not be treated as a fully verified list of instructors for a particular semester.

Faculty profiles, LinkedIn pages and course offerings can change. Some instructors may teach only selected terms, and sample courses may not all be offered in a given semester. A LinkedIn search link is not itself confirmation of a person's identity or profile.

The next stage should be a semester-specific verification of course sections and instructors, followed by deeper research into their academic histories, professional experience, teaching materials and relevant publications.
